simple.meaning: רֵו (rêv) is a Hebrew word meaning “aspect.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רֵו (H7299) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:31, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֵו (H7299) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in רֵו (H7299) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: רֵו (rêv) / H7299 is traced through Daniel 2:31, Daniel 3:25 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “You, O king, saw, and behold,* “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its appearance was terrifying.

timeline.evidenceText: “You, O king, saw, and behold,* “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its appearance was terrifying.
He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”
